chunk_findings.detail: The manifest lists `tests/test_lease_contest.py` as deleted and lists no replacement module or package at that path among the 9 changed files. This removes the old import path required by the stated conformance and [r-small-files]; after the change, any code, pin, or pytest node id that refers to `tests.test_lease_contest` / `tests/test_lease_contest.py::...` will fail because that module no longer exists. The split should preserve the old path as a compatibility module/package rather than deleting it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `_Seq` is documented as “a step list that collects the claims its resolutions released,” but `gone: set[str]` is only a class annotation and no `__init__` initializes an instance attribute. In `_run`, the collection happens through `getattr(seq, "gone", set()).add(...)`, so when `seq` has no real `gone` attribute, `getattr` creates a fresh set, adds to that temporary object, and discards it. For example, `seq = _Seq([("acq", "alice"), ("acq", "bob"), ("res", 0)])` followed by `_run(claims, seq)` leaves `seq` without `gone`; reading `seq.gone` raises `AttributeError`, and the claims released by the resolution are not recorded. Tests that rely on `_Seq` to collect released claims either fail or, if they use `getattr(seq, "gone", set())`, can pass vacuously with an empty set.
chunk_findings.title: tests/lease_contest_support.py:107 (`_Seq`) / tests/lease_contest_support.py:101 (`_run`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and does not leave a shim/facade, so the old file/import path no longer exists. The intent explicitly requires that the split “keeps the old import path” and warns about golden/pin references to the file. After the change, `pytest tests/test_lease_contest.py` fails with “file or directory not found”, and any CI command, pin, or golden that names the old test file path breaks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: Splitting the tests into new modules changes every collected pytest node id from `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_...` to `tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py::test_...` (and similar for the other new modules). The supplied change contains no documented rename map from old ids to new ids. A CI check or golden file comparing collected ids will therefore fail: e.g. the old id `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_every_claim_that_overlapped_another_stays_in_the_contest[alice-bob-carol]` is no longer collected, while the new id in `tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py` is not in the expected set. The intent requires the collected ids to be the same set or documented with a rename map.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted) / tests/test_lease_contest_*.py

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_renewal_of_the_fresh_lease_does_not_stretch_the_original` cannot run as written: the generator iterates over `h` (`for h in it.displaced`) but its predicate references undefined `e` (`e["holder"] == "D"`). When pytest executes this test, the call to `next(...)` raises `NameError: name 'e' is not defined`, so the test is effectively dropped/weakens the split rather than preserving the original coverage.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_fresh_window.py:78

chunk_findings.detail: The split removes the old test module and moves its tests into new modules without preserving the collected test-id set or providing a documented rename map. For example, a test that previously collected as `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_every_claim_that_overlapped_another_stays_in_the_contest[bob-carol-alice]` now collects as `tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py::test_every_claim_that_overlapped_another_stays_in_the_contest[bob-carol-alice]`. The manifest shows no old-path shim or rename-map file, so any golden/pin or test-id comparison that names the old file fails, violating the explicit split conformance requirement [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The property test makes the generated event sequence depend on Python set iteration order. It builds `seq.gone` as a set and then iterates `for w in list(seq.gone):` to insert releases. For string names, set iteration order is not stable across runs unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is fixed; the same `seed` can process the same `gone` set in different orders. Because each iteration calls `rnd.randrange(...)`, the random stream is consumed differently, changing the inserted release positions and all later `res`/`hold`/`at` choices. Thus the test is nondeterministic and can pass in one environment and fail in another for the same parameterized seed, weakening the intended regression coverage.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_release.py:test_releases_in_any_position_leave_the_contest_exact

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and moves its tests to new module paths, so pytest collected ids necessarily change; for example, an old id such as `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_a_holders_own_reclaim_keeps_its_first_claim_on_record` becomes `tests/test_lease_contest_renewal.py::test_a_holders_own_reclaim_keeps_its_first_claim_on_record`. The manifest contains no old-path shim and no rename map/golden update (only a baseline line removal and a one-line edit to `test_release_paths.py`), so any golden/pin or CI selection that names the old file or old node ids will collect zero tests, violating the operator requirement that collected ids stay the same or be documented and that the split keep the old import path [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_renewal.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and redirects the helper import to `lease_contest_support`, but the stated conformance for this change requires that a split keep the old import path and preserve the collected test-id set, or provide a documented rename map. After this change, tests that previously had ids such as `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_a_late_claim_inside_the_kept_claims_real_tenure_is_still_a_contest` are collected under new file paths like `tests/test_lease_contest_fresh_window.py::test_a_late_claim_inside_the_kept_claims_real_tenure_is_still_a_contest`, and `tests.test_lease_contest` is no longer importable. No compatibility shim or rename map is included, so this breaks any golden/pin or external caller that references the old file/path and violates [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_release_paths.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: The intent requires the split to keep the old import path, but the manifest deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and adds only sibling modules (`tests/test_lease_contest_fresh_window.py`, `tests/test_lease_contest_keep_holder.py`, `tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py`, `tests/test_lease_contest_release.py`, `tests/test_lease_contest_renewal.py`) and `tests/lease_contest_support.py`; there is no `tests/test_lease_contest.py` shim or `tests/test_lease_contest/__init__.py` package. Given `python -c 'import tests.test_lease_contest'`, the import succeeds before the change and fails with `ModuleNotFoundError` after it, so the split does not keep the old import path as required by [r-small-files].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `_Seq` declares `gone: set[str]` only as a type annotation; it never initializes the attribute (there is no `__init__` and no `gone = set()`). `_run` uses `getattr(seq, "gone", set()).add(h["holder"])`, which on a fresh `_Seq` creates and discards a temporary set instead of storing it on `seq`. So a test using the documented `_Seq` collection, e.g. `seq = _Seq([...]); _run(..., seq); seq.gone`, will raise `AttributeError` and lose the released-claim collection.
chunk_findings.title: tests/lease_contest_support.py:_Seq

chunk_findings.detail: The deleted `tests/test_lease_contest.py` release section in this part contains exactly five test functions: `test_a_release_that_ends_a_contest_keeps_the_claims_left_on_record`, `test_releasing_the_displayed_contestant_displays_the_latest_left`, `test_releases_in_any_position_leave_the_contest_exact`, `test_resolve_keeps_every_claim_it_did_not_release_on_record`, and `test_resolve_leaves_bystanders_that_met_each_other_contested`. The manifest says the new `tests/test_lease_contest_release.py` adds the first four “and 2 more”, i.e. six test functions. That is an extra test id not present in the old module and not covered by a documented rename map, violating the change’s own requirement that the collected test-id set before and after be the same (or a documented rename map). [r-small-files]
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_release.py

chunk_findings.detail: The split re-homes every test from `tests/test_lease_contest.py` under new module paths such as `tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py`, so the collected pytest node IDs are not the same set before and after. The change includes no rename-map file, and the new file's docstring only says it was split from the old file rather than mapping old node IDs to new node IDs. This violates the change's stated requirement that collected test IDs be the same set or have a documented rename map, so any golden or pin that names `tests/test_lease_contest.py::...` will break.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py

chunk_findings.detail: The `ids` callable receives the full parameter-set tuple, for example `({...}, "K", ("A", "B", ...))` for the `_KEEP_FAR` case. Because `v` is a tuple, the callable executes `"-".join(v)`; the first element is a `dict`, so `str.join` raises `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, dict found` while pytest builds test IDs. Running `pytest tests/test_lease_contest_release.py` therefore fails collection for `test_resolve_keeps_every_claim_it_did_not_release_on_record`, and the parametrized test is not collected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_release.py:93

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and moves its tests into new module paths such as `tests/test_lease_contest_renewal.py`, so the old import path `tests.test_lease_contest` no longer exists and each collected pytest node id changes (e.g. the old `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_a_holders_own_reclaim_keeps_its_first_claim_on_record` becomes `tests/test_lease_contest_renewal.py::...`). The manifest shows no shim module or documented rename map to satisfy the stated `r-small-files` conformance requirement that the split keep the old import path and preserve the same collected test ids, so a golden/pin or CI selector naming `tests/test_lease_contest.py` now fails to collect/import.

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest deletes the module at the old import path and adds no replacement file or package at `tests/test_lease_contest.py`; therefore any existing import, pytest selection, or golden/pin that still references that path fails immediately (for example, `pytest tests/test_lease_contest.py` or `import tests.test_lease_contest` now errors with `ModuleNotFoundError`/collection error). This violates the stated split requirement, and [r-small-files], that a split keeps the old import path and changes no behaviour.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `_Seq` only annotates `gone` (`gone: set[str]`) but never initializes it, and `_run` records released claims with `getattr(seq, "gone", set()).add(...)`. When `seq` has no `gone` attribute, that expression mutates a throwaway set. For example, with `seq = _Seq([("acq", "a"), ("acq", "b"), ("res", 0)])` and overlapping claims `{"a": (0.0, 10), "b": (5.0, 10)}`, `_run` resolves the contest and releases one holder, but `seq.gone` raises `AttributeError` and `getattr(seq, "gone", set())` is empty. The helper therefore does not collect releases as its docstring says.
chunk_findings.title: tests/lease_contest_support.py:_Seq

chunk_findings.detail: `_resolved` hard-codes release Lamports as `20 + i` and the resolution Lamport as `30`. Given 13 overlapping claims, e.g. `claims = {f"h{i}": (0.0, 10) for i in range(13)}`, `order=tuple(claims)`, `keep="h0"`, there are 12 losers; the last release event gets Lamport 31 while the resolution gets Lamport 30. Since folding orders by Lamport, the resolution is applied before the last loser release, contrary to the documented “releases, then resolution.” With 19 or more acquisitions, release Lamports also collide with acquisition Lamports.
chunk_findings.title: tests/lease_contest_support.py:_resolved

chunk_findings.detail: The split changes the collected pytest node ids: before the tests were collected under `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_...`, now they are collected under `tests/test_lease_contest_fresh_window.py::test_...`, `tests/test_lease_contest_keep_holder.py::test_...`, etc. The change includes no documented rename map, so the requirement that the collected test ids before and after be the same set (or have a documented rename map) is violated; any golden or pin that names the old file path will fail.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted) and new test modules

chunk_findings.detail: Deleting `tests/test_lease_contest.py` without a compatibility shim or re-export module means `import tests.test_lease_contest` now raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. This violates the conformance statement that a split “keeps the old import path,” so any code, tooling, or test selection that still imports the old test module breaks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: Deleting tests/test_lease_contest.py and splitting it into tests/test_lease_contest_keep_holder.py changes pytest node ids (for example `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_resolve_can_keep_the_holder_that_took_over_after_a_double_claim[...]` no longer exists as a collected id). The change has no documented old→new test-id rename map, so any golden or pin that names the original file will now fail collection, contrary to the stated split requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and adds split modules such as this one, with no compatibility shim or documented rename map in the manifest. The old import path `tests.test_lease_contest` is gone, and every collected node id for these tests changes, e.g. `tests/test_lease_contest.py::test_every_claim_that_overlapped_another_stays_in_the_contest` will no longer match any test. This violates the stated requirement that collected test ids before and after be the same set (or have a documented rename map) and “keeps the old import path”.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest.py

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring says this test guards against the regression where the summary says all four claims were “claimed at once”, but the body never calls `contest_summary()` or `run_cli("show")`; it only checks `it.lease_contest` holders and `it.lease_clashes`. Given `_GROUPS` (two disjoint groups) with a buggy `contest_summary()` that still emits “claimed at once by alice and bob and carol and dave”, both assertions still pass, so the advertised regression is not actually caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_overlap.py:test_two_groups_that_never_met_are_named_apart

chunk_findings.detail: The `ids=lambda v: "-".join(v) if isinstance(v, tuple) else ...` in the parametrize decorator for `test_resolve_keeps_every_claim_it_did_not_release_on_record` is called by pytest with the full parameter tuple `(_KEEP_FAR, "K", order_tuple)` (and likewise `(_GROUPS, "alice", order_tuple)`). Because the first element is a dict, `"-".join(v)` raises `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, dict found` during test collection. This makes the new test module fail to collect rather than run the split release tests.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lease_contest_release.py:93

chunk_findings.detail: The split deletes `tests/test_lease_contest.py` and retargets the importer in `tests/test_release_paths.py` to `lease_contest_support`, so the previously existing import path `from test_lease_contest import _REPRO, _acq, _ev` is gone. That contradicts the change intent requirement that the split “keeps the old import path”; any other consumer (for example a CI pin or helper script named in the intent that still uses the old path) now fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'test_lease_contest'`.
